newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran expects "rational" EU stance - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iran expects "rational" EU stance - paper.

text.p: Iran expects European Union foreign ministers to take a rational stance at their meeting next week to pave the way for cooperation with the Islamic republic, a leading Tehran newspaper said on Sunday.
Neither Iran nor the EU wanted deterioration in relations, said the Tehran Times in an editorial on the withdrawal of EU ambassadors in a crisis over political killings in Europe.
"Basically there is an understanding between the two sides that Iran-EU cordial ties are in both sides' interests," the English-language daily said.

EU nations, except Greece, withdrew their ambassadors from Iran after a German court ruled on April 10 that Iran's rulers ordered the killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Tehran has repeatedly denied any involvement in the killings.
The newspaper praised statements by the German and French foreign ministers, Klaus Kinkel and Herve de Charette, which stressed maintaining ties with Iran.
Kinkel said on Thursday it was imperative to maintain links with Tehran.
De Charette was quoted as saying on Friday France wished to have a mutually beneficial dialogue with Iran and its people. EU nations would soon send ambassadors back to Tehran, he said.
Tehran Times said the statements indicated Europe had realised Iran's key role in the region and was determined to maintain cordial ties with Iran.
"Without any doubt Iran too does not want a crisis in its ties with the EU provided European countries realise the sensitivity of our people to any sacrilege of our values," the paper said.
The Iranian nation expected the EU foreign ministers to take a rational stance in their meeting on April 29-30, it said.
"Any irrational stance by the EU foreign ministers will definitely serve the interests of the Zionists and the U.S. which will be virtually to the detriment of the European countries," it added.
